meta.title: Novogradac LIHTC Equity Pricing Benchmarks
meta.source_publisher: Novogradac LIHTC equity pricing pages (Affordable Housing Resource Center)
meta.methodology: Novogradac compiles syndicator letter-of-intent (LOI) pricing from market participants. National: the average LOI price for 9% and 4% credits each month, averaged here over the quarter's three months. Regional and state: Novogradac's published median for the quarter, all credit types together (it splits 9% and 4% only where it has enough data, currently California and New York). Pricing is dollars of equity per dollar of tax credit; no adjustment for timing of capital contributions.
meta.important_disclaimer: Benchmarks are Novogradac's published averages and medians, which are market context, not a quote. For IC memos, investor presentations or capital-stack sizing, get a current letter of intent from a syndicator: individual deals price several cents either side of these figures on location, sponsor, deal size and investor demand.
meta.update_cadence: Quarterly. Novogradac's Q2 2026 regional page was live by 2026-10-08, about one quarter after the quarter ended, so a current snapshot is normally 90–200 days past its as_of. scripts/audit/equity-pricing-watch.mjs opens a capture reminder when next_expected_update is near.

capture_pages.title: Regional and State-Level LIHTC Equity Pricing

national_avg.notes: Average of Novogradac's April, May and June 2026 monthly national averages (9%: $0.82, $0.82, $0.81; 4%: $0.83, $0.84, $0.82). 4% credits priced above 9% this quarter, as they did in 2025-Q3; through 2024 the two were within about a cent. CohnReznick's October 2026 monitor attributes the 2026 softness partly to added supply from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's larger 9% allocations and lower 4% bond test.

CO.label: Colorado
CO.notes: Novogradac's Colorado median for Q2 2026, all credit types. It does not publish Denver, rural or resort figures, or a 9%/4% split for Colorado.

pricing.regional_notes: Regional and state figures are Novogradac's medians for the quarter across 9% and 4% credits together; credit_9pct/credit_4pct are null where Novogradac does not split them. States are listed only where Novogradac had enough data to publish a median.

what_moves_pricing_up: Falling 10y Treasury yield (debt becomes cheaper → cap rates fall → residual value rises → investor IRR up)
CRA reform creating new buyer demand
Tax-credit policy certainty (e.g., extending placed-in-service windows, raising 9% credit cap)
Permanent 100% bonus depreciation under Section 168(k) for qualified property acquired after January 19, 2025 (Public Law 119-21, section 70301)
Strong sponsor track record (CHFA-allocator-tier syndicators get premium)
Larger deals (50+ units, $20M+ TDC) get premium of 1-2 cents over smaller
what_moves_pricing_down: Tax-rate cut concerns (lower top-rate = lower credit value)
Rural / smaller / first-time-sponsor / non-traditional populations discount

validation_check.verified_against: Novogradac 'LIHTC Equity Pricing Trends' and 'Regional and State-Level LIHTC Equity Pricing' pages (both as of Q2 2026), saved from a browser on 2026-10-08; Public Law 119-21 section 70301 for Section 168(k) bonus depreciation treatment
validation_check.next_review: Quarterly. scripts/audit/equity-pricing-watch.mjs (monthly workflow) opens a capture reminder before next_expected_update and a drift issue when CohnReznick's median sits more than 2¢ outside the national range.
validation_check.ingestion_note: novoco.com answers scripted requests with a Cloudflare challenge, so capture is by hand from saved pages. The trends chart is vector: each bar's height reads exactly against the axis gridlines.
validation_check.cross_check: CohnReznick Tax Credit Advisor Housing Tax Credit Monitor, October 2026: surveyed median net equity price $0.823 across 93 properties, June–July 2026 (https://www.taxcreditadvisor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/TCA-Housing-Tax-Credit-Monitor_October_2026.pdf). Closed-deal median, a different measure, within 1¢ of the national range above.

state_qap_pricing.summary: Colorado's QAP publishes no equity price: CHFA sets an equity factor in the Preliminary Application or uses the applicant's letter of interest. Of Colorado's North Central neighbors and Utah, New Mexico and Nebraska are the only plans with a number. New Mexico's recommended $0.85–$0.95 and Nebraska's $0.85 template both sit above Novogradac's Q2 2026 medians ($0.80 North Central, $0.81 Colorado, $0.82 Southwest). Underwriting at either figure would overstate equity at current market pricing.
state_qap_pricing.not_verified: Arizona's 2026 ranges ($0.77–$0.84 Maricopa/Pima, $0.75–$0.81 other counties, $0.74–$0.83 tribal land) appear only in secondary summaries; housing.az.gov refused scripted requests, so they are not recorded here.

entries.name: Colorado (CHFA)
entries.quote: CHFA will select, at least annually, an equity factor based on market conditions. At the time of the Preliminary Application, the equity factor to be used for this calculation is listed in the Preliminary Application. If there is a Letter of Interest or a firm equity commitment in place at this time, use the equity factor contained in the Letter of Interest or commitment.
entries.note: The 2026 Housing Tax Credit Application (V8.2, May 2026) leaves the federal, state and TOC equity factors as blank applicant inputs with no minimum or maximum; the 2027-2028 QAP third draft keeps the same text but changes 'will select' to 'may select'. No state AHTC price is stated.

entries.name: New Mexico (Housing New Mexico)
entries.quote: Housing New Mexico has a recommended range of credit of $.85 and $.95 for the credit pricing factor and will underwrite the Project using the factor contained in the letter of interest (LOI)
entries.note: A recommended range, not a floor: the project is underwritten at its letter-of-intent price. The draft 2027 supplement repeats it.

entries.name: Nebraska (NIFA)
entries.quote: Divided by Net Equity Factor $ 0.8500 (Current dollar yield of net syndication proceeds per dollar of LIHTC)
entries.note: Shown on a sample form, not stated as a requirement. Federal LIHTC has no minimum price; a quoted range must be no wider than $0.05. The state AHTC requires 'equity pricing of $0.60 or greater' (Exhibit 116).

entries.name: Utah (UHC)
entries.quote: UHC will underwrite projects assuming Housing Credit pricing that reflects current local pricing trends.

entries.name: Montana (MBOH)
entries.quote: Letter of interest with the anticipated price based on the market at time of the Application.

entries.name: Kansas (KHRC)
entries.quote: KHRC may use the price outlined in the excel application for both the Federal and State LIHTCs to evaluate the proposal, provided the price reasonably reflects current market conditions.

entries.name: South Dakota (SDHDA)
entries.quote: SDHDA will establish a base market rate expressed in cents netted per dollar of credit allocation. The Market Rate will be set for each individual project
entries.note: Set per project by the agency; no published figure.
